antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:20 — the lock has a fixed 6h TTL. If a run ever goes past that, the lock expires silently and a manual run could overlap (low risk at this TTL).

tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php:34 — re-declaring #[Signature] on an anonymous subclass to force confirmation is a workaround. If the real signature changes, this copy can drift without anyone noticing. The docblock explains why it is needed, though.

tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php — no test where the disk throws an exception (only the case where delete returns false), no test for a row whose file is already gone, and no test that crosses the 1000-row chunk boundary of lazyById.
strengths: The command uses its own Cache::lock rather than relying on the scheduler's withoutOverlapping. That correctly covers both servers and manual runs. The lock is taken only after confirmation and released in a finally block.
Uses ConfirmableTrait, so the production check and --force behave as the framework normally does. Refusing returns FAILURE.
Rows are streamed with lazyById, which is safe to delete from while iterating and keeps memory flat on millions of rows. Adds an index on created_at for the scope.
Validates --days with filter_var and min_range, and returns a failure code for bad values.
Catches exceptions from the disk, reports them and keeps going. Removed and failed counts are printed, and the exit code is FAILURE if anything failed.
Uses modern conventions: #[Signature]/#[Description], #[Scope], #[Fillable], and a typed factory with a createdDaysAgo state. Adds the inverse User::exports relation.
Production tests really switch the environment with detectEnvironment, including dry-run in production. The scheduler test checks the cron expression, onOneServer and --force.

bugs: app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:21 — the lock TTL is only 1h. Deleting files one at a time over a few million rows can easily take longer than that. The lock then expires mid-run and a manual or second-server run could start alongside it, which is exactly what the task asked to prevent.
antipatterns: routes/console.php:14 — withoutOverlapping(60) is redundant with the command's own cache lock, and its 60-minute mutex expiry has the same too-short problem.
app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:36,60 — mixes $this->info() with $this->components->error(), so output styling is inconsistent.
app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:45 — a comment that restates what the lock does.

tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php:37-47 — the helper inProduction() never sets the environment to production. It only swaps in a subclass that always asks for confirmation, so the name is misleading. As a result test_dry_run_needs_no_confirmation_in_production (line 108) never runs in production and only checks the exit code: it doesn't check the output or that nothing was deleted.
tests/Feature/PurgeExportsTest.php:40 — re-declares #[Signature] on an anonymous subclass, which can drift from the real one.
strengths: The core design matches impl-1: ConfirmableTrait, a Cache::lock taken after confirmation and released in finally, lazyById streaming, catching exceptions from the disk, a FAILURE exit code, and an index on created_at.
The scope takes an explicit cutoff (CarbonInterface), and the query builder is built once and reused for both the count and the purge.

Tests cover more cases: disk returns false and disk throws in the same run, a missing file still deletes its row, more than one chunk (1200 rows), dry-run ignores the lock, several invalid --days values, disk config, and scheduler flags including withoutOverlapping.
Refusing without a terminal is tested by actually setting env to production with --no-interaction.

v.rationale: I ranked impl-1 first, narrowly. The two implementations are almost the same design, and both test suites pass (impl-1: 16 tests, impl-2: 20). My probes gave the same results on both: a disk that throws keeps its row and fails the run, a real permission-denied delete keeps its row and the rest are purged, 1500 rows cross the lazyById chunk boundary correctly, a row exactly 30 days old is kept, and --days with trailing whitespace works. Both correctly use a cache lock inside the command, which is what actually stops a manual run overlapping the nightly one. Three things separate them. First, impl-2's lock TTL is 1h, and its withoutOverlapping(60) is redundant. On a few million rows with one file delete each, a run can outlast that and the lock expires silently. impl-1 uses 6h. Second, impl-2's helper inProduction() never sets production, so its 'dry-run in production' test is mislabelled and checks almost nothing. impl-1 really switches the environment. Third, impl-2 mixes info() and components output. impl-2's tests do cover more edge cases (disk throwing, missing file, chunking, dry-run with the lock held), which keeps it close, but the lock duration matters more for this task's focus on safe operation.
